utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good morning to you as well, Mr. Liborius. Same procedure that you're reminded that you're still bound by the solemn declaration that you gave at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Misetic, are you ready to continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Liborius.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sir, following up on our discussion yesterday, you gave us some names on a sheet of paper. But in reviewing the transcript I noted that you also mentioned that you maintain contact with some of your ECMM colleagues. Could you tell us the names of the ECMM colleagues from that time-period with whom you remain in contact?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did discuss with Stig Marker-Hansen and Eric Hendriks. However, I have not had contacts with them in the recent time. Just a correction of your maintain contact, could indicate that we have a long contact even today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us when the discussions with Mr. Marker-Hansen and Mr. Hendriks took place?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It took place in 1995. I met Mr. Marker-Hansen again in 1996, 1997, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Any time after 1997?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, that's difficult to say. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And what about Mr. Hendriks?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't had contact with Mr. Eric Hendriks for many years. So the last time would be in our ECMM years, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I could have 1D50-0382, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, on your screen you see a bus. Do you recall ever seeing a bus like this during your time at the monitoring mission?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly that type of model and bus or the Promet -- I did see the Promet sign on some of the buses. In general, they were often older mark. When has that picture been taken?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This picture is undated. But my question to you is: You saw the Promet. Do you recall also seeing that the buses would sometimes be marked by the cities from which the bus line operated? For example, on the back end of the bus it says Split Hrvatska or Split Croatia?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember that there were some inscriptions on the buses, names of cities, sometimes, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me draw your attention, right now -- Madam Registrar [sic], if we could have -- D743 on the screen, please. This is your notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, Mr. Registrar, I apologise. And, Mr. Registrar, if we could go to the page marked on the bottom right-hand corner as 1D50-0253.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Liborius, this is your notebook entry for 24 August. And if you see -- it says Grahovo there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Could you read that out for us and tell us what you found, based on your notes, when you were in Grahovo?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I read my notes it says: Grahovo, buses, trucks, other vehicles, 10/10, large, Split buses resting en route, receiving mail, different units, CUMDR, abbreviation for commander. Receiving large envelopes, minus heavy, or minus engineer equip, abbreviation for equipment, reorganisation HVO, MO, HV.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you again you said reorganisation where it very much looks as if it is a "G" at the end is that because it is Danish or is it "reorganising" or is it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Foreign language spoken]... is in Danish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now the entry "Split buses," as you sit here today do you know if you were able to identify the buses as being from Split on the basis of the plates or on the basis of the buses as I just showed you a picture that it said Split on the buses. Can you tell from your notes?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do I write in the daily report?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you right now if you could tell on the basis of your notes.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of my notes, probably it would be a combination of number plates and writings on the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now if we could go to P813, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, this is the daily report for that same day. If we go down to military situation. And you can read that to yourself for a minute, and tell me when you finish reading that portion.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have read the military situation, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you note that when you prepared the daily report or whoever prepared the daily report at the end of the day, instead of writing that the vehicles were from HVO/HV, Mostar and Split, it instead says Zadar and Sibenik with no mention of Split. And I was wondering if you could explain to us why in your notes it says the buses were from Split and in the daily report it is Zadar and Sibenik, without any reference to Split?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said before, it could very well be that there had been Split writings on the wall -- on the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender the picture of the buses as a Defence exhibit, 1D50-0382.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit number D754.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D754 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar, I'm going to call up with an exhibit which I think the Prosecution has tendered but it still has no P number, so we can assign a P number to it right now. It is 65 ter 5435, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit number P828.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see this on my list as translation requested. Is there a translation already?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's not the document I'm trying to call up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have an ECMM special report, 3rd of October. Yes, that's the one. That appears on my list where it's the -- the number is handwritten.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, I'll call it up by a different 65 ter number then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'll move on to that topic in a moment, Your Honour, while we find the document. Your Honour, for the moment we will show it via Sanction just so we don't waste time, but it is a 65 ter exhibit as well. And I will later come back and tender it as the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, if you can look at your screen this is an ECMM special report. At the end it is signed by Mr. Sanchez Rau -- or not signed but --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see any document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn to the tenth paragraph of this report, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, I believe I found the document. It is 65 ter 2378.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It is on page 4 of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us who Mr. Sanchez Rau was, Mr. Liborius?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Head of mission, ECMM.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And in the hierarchy, where would that place him?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Top.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Top, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could go to page four, please, in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: There under the section on burning, Mr. Sanchez Rau writes: "Throughout the Krajina, houses were burnt and even today, more than five weeks after the last fighting, they are still being burnt. The large-scale destruction of non-Croat property may lead to the conclusion that it has not only been done by marauding gangs or that it has at least been tolerated by the Croatian authorities." My question to you, sir, is can you help us understand what "the marauding gangs" refers to?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Marauding gangs" will have been a word that Mr. Sanchez Rau had decided to use. I don't recall using such a fancy word, not usually in my vocabulary. But if you, here in 2008, ask my opinion about marauding gangs, my position now, I'm prepared to do so. Should I do that, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, let me ask it a different way. You testified on direct examination that the issue of warlords was not even something that was discussed at the time. Now, this doesn't say "warlords" but it says "marauding gangs," and I'm wondering if you recall discussions within the ECMM about marauding gangs causing burning and looting?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have marauding gangs in my discussions. I did pronounce myself a couple of days ago regarding warlords. I'm not sure what your question would entail.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Marauding gangs in this context seems to suggest some sort of -- I don't want to mischaracterize it, but seems to suggest groups of people who are just roaming the area and causing problems. And in the context it says: "It is not only been done by marauding gangs or that it has at least been tolerated by Croatian authorities," and I was hoping that perhaps you could enlighten us as to what the reference to marauding gangs is. Marauding gangs referred to what groups?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, two observations. If you want to know what Mr. Sanchez Rau meant by choosing the words "marauding gangs," you really have to ask himself. Second observation, if you ask for my description as to who committed these burnings, I'm prepared to give you the explanation. It would very much look like the one I have repeated at several instances.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, we don't need you to repeat anything.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: What I do need you, though, to tell me is where you said on direct that you don't recall the issue of warlords being discussed, do you recall the issuing of marauding gangs being discussed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I think the witness answered the previous question, "Marauding gangs -- I did not have marauding gangs in my discussions."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Fine. As long as that's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: When Mr. Sanchez Rau prepared reports, was it customary that he would rely on what observers in the field had discovered and then compile the reports that would be sent to wherever they were being sent to?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Sanchez Rau was the head of the ECMM, at the top of the organisation. So he would rely on input from different elements in his staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender this exhibit into evidence, please. Actually, it's a P exhibit so if we could get a P number for it --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number P829.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P829 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could have P819 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that, the word "marauding" and "to maraud" was totally unknown to me, and I understand it now to be to rove and raid in search of plunder. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I didn't know it either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: P819. If we could scroll down. If we could go to 3a, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, it says: "Apart from two large detonations in the afternoon, probably demolition, the K1 AOR is calm but with most of the active military units and equipment employed in Bosnia-Herzegovina." Could you tell us a little bit more about this sentence about active military units and equipment being employed in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you scroll to the top please, again. Could you scroll down again, please. If I could tell you a little bit more about active military units and equipment being employed in Bosnia-Herzegovina, yes, the HVO and the HV operated side by side. The HV operated - it was my understanding - under the provisions of the so-called Split Agreement between the Croatian president Tudjman and Alija Izetbegovic of Bosnia. That provided the legal basis for Croatian units in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And it was your assessment that most of the activity military units and equipment were employed in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we observed in our area of responsibility was that the larger units were not visible to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And we -- as we say in the report, saw that most of the active military units and equipment were employed in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could scroll down, staying right there. You talk about --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But as the report continues: "For the more comprehensive and detailed military picture it is recommended to attend to the UNMO reporting. This information remains by far the best source of military information as local Croatian authorities refuse to answer specific questions if they are asked ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, read the top of that. And it continued from the previous page: "... would be ... jeopardized if K1, still with limited resources, are turned into a MILINFO gathering agency. K1 does not possess the manpower either in terms of quantity of skills nor the necessary equipment." Tell us what MILINFO is first?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And was there any kind of request to the ECMM to have the ECMM do MILINFO gathering that triggered this entry in this daily report?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a standing point on the agenda of the ECMM monitoring provided for in the original mandate to also report on military information. I would gather that there would have been a discussion, perhaps, inside the organisation as if there could be more focus on military information or less. I would really need to see more paper suggesting this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's turn then to D741, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're doing that, K1 is one of the units of the monitoring mission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Team Kilo 1, yes, Knin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Knin 1. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: 741, please. If we could turn to page 14 of the transcript, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Liborius, for the entry on Saturday, 19 August, from your diary you wrote: "RC meeting in Zadar. We get almost all our ideas approved. It doesn't touch our work area, to the contrary, we are praised for our efforts so far. But on the question of patrolling in HVO parts of Bosnia, the HRC goes (completely) into the air. What an incompetent neurotic mannequin." Now why did the HRC go completely into the air on the question of patrolling in HVO parts of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could with we go to private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I don't know why so -- sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The problem always is that if it's explained in public session then the harm might be done. We turn into private session for you to explain why we have to deal with the matter in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I notice that it's 10.30. We'll have a break. We will resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic. Mr. Liborius, we will continue. We are in open session again. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In light of the witness's answer before the break, my team has pulled a document which is not in e-court which we will show in Sanction and upload in e-court to show the witness. We've just sent a copy to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And for the Chamber ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It will be on Sanction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be on Sanction, yes. Mr. Liborius.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I just have a question as I'm not fully familiar with the procedures of this Court. I presume that my remarks from the private session will not later be reproduced by either the Defence or the Prosecutor in open session and also not with another witness or another session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They will not be referred to -- I mean, what is said in private session is to be kept confidential. If there would ever be a need to raise an issue with another witness, that other witness would, first of all, be instructed that he should keep it confidential. But I do understand your concerns, who would be that other witness and under what circumstances. Of course, then Mr. Waespi will be in a position to raise the issue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What really is my question is what is the character of the protections of this information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you're discussing this in open session and I don't know whether that is what you prefer to do. The Victims and Witness Section is perfectly able to explain to you procedural matters, because Mr. Waespi is not in a position at this moment to speak with you. If there are any concerns in that respect, please first address the Victims and Witness Section. If there is any need, then, to liaise with the Chamber or the parties, the Victims and Witness Unit will do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, we've just retrieved this document. I'd ask you to review it. This is a document dated 28 August 1995, from HRC Knin, and it talks about the boundaries for the various teams. If could you look through that document. Tell me when you need us to scroll down.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please scroll a bit down. Please scroll down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That is the end of the document.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please scroll up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay? Now, from this document it says in section 2: "Basic grounds were to monitor the situation in the previous RSK (human rights of the remaining Serbs) as well as in the previous free Croatia part of the AOR. POW, possible trials with, however, an emphasised focus on the former UN Sector South." It then goes on, it says that basically the same thing, the mission in section 1: Subordinated to RC Zagreb, four teams, Gospic, Zadar, and Dubrovnik. CC Split has now to assess the consequences of the war and in the former RSK territories and in the former free Croatia territories. Section 2, third point is: "Stick as much as possible to the Croat administrative boundaries." And then section 3 relates: Teams to internal Republic of Croatia county boundaries. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In section 3. The terms, for example --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very poorly visible here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with what the term "Zupanja" means?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The administrative district.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So, the teams then were being -- their areas of responsibility were related to the Croat administrative districts. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a general rule, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You were asked previously about what the orders were for where you were to go. There is nothing in this order talking about, Team Knin can go into Bosnia, is there?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: There's nothing in the order that says, Team Knin can go and patrol in Bosnia, does it?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender this exhibit, 1D50-0395 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could I attach a comment to this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, first of all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. I have no objection. Also I missed the word "order" in the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You'd say from -- face value it is not an order. But -- let's -- I mean, the Chamber can read it. Of course, we have heard the evidence also from this witness earlier that -- that the mandate was broader and not limited by the borders. There's no objection, Mr. Waespi. Therefore, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number D754.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Liborius, there's a document and what Mr. Misetic asked you does not appear in that document. That's all. I don't know -- if you want to add one word, please do so. But it is just as simple as that. We have -- Mr. Misetic doesn't ask you to draw any conclusions, whether at any stage in the totality of the evidence Mr. Misetic will ask us to draw conclusions, we'll hear that from him. At this moment we're not -- if you want to add a word, please do so, briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, apologies for the interruption. I have a correction to make. The last exhibit should be D755.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D755 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Registrar, if I could go back to D741, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if we could now go to the entry for 23 August, which is on page 16. Mr. Liborius, I'm going to show you three diary entries now, and let me go through the three diary entries and then I'll pose a question to you about them. If you look at 23 August, towards the middle you write: "Around Drvar and Trebinje," which are two towns in Bosnia, correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "There continues to be built up, CRO waits because of US pressure."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Then if we can turn the page -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Continuing on, you say you met with the commander in Benkovac. You go on and say: "I wish him and his men few losses and a fair fight down in Trebinje." Which, again as you've said, is a town in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Here you describe your visit to Grahovo and you write: "We decide to go into Grahovo. I'm sure something must be going on in there. And yes, of course, as expected Grahovo is being used as an inner front line junction. Then you describe what you saw. And you say: "It was a victory to have it confirmed that the HV/HVO building will move to Drvar and Trebinje in order to pressure BSA." BSA means Bosnian Serb army, correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Flip forward to page 20 which is your entry for 30 August, second sentence: "We get reports of some push towards Drvar from the HV." Now, sir, my question to you is, you were aware, were you not, in August, towards the end of August that the HV was engaged in Bosnia in combat. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That the HV was engaged at the end of August in Bosnia followed from the Split declaration. It is hardly a military secret, so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn the page, please, to go to the September 1 entry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, here it says you went to Donji Lapac and then it says: "There is fighting going on here with the HV/BSA over the border so there are only 18 Serbs in the whole municipality, the rest only soldiers and police." When you actually physically went up to Donji Lapac, sir, can you tell us how you were able to determine that fighting was going on on the other side of the border between the Bosnian Serb army and the HV? Did you see it?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you flip to the daily report of the 1st September, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That would be P818, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you scroll down, please. Could you scroll up, please. Yes, please. How we were able to determine the fighting was going on, on the other side of the border, I remember that the chief of police, as indicated in the report, provided information to that effect, and we saw rear units, water bladders logistic vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Return for a moment to a different topic. You say on one of the videos that we saw that you personally witnessed soldiers with fuel cans in the Drnis area on the 10th of August setting fire to houses. First, can you tell us who you were with on the 10th of August when you saw this?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you flip to the 10 August report, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I think that might be 65 ter 4048.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Before we scroll through this, I do want to ask you if you actually recall the incident without looking at the report.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The incident about the fuel canisters?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one where the burning took place when you go down from the road and the entire right-hand side in the direction down to Knin, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Scroll down, please. Scroll down, please. Next page, please. Scroll down, please. That's the RC report so we're not on the team report. But off the top of my head, the incident, and I would prefer to see the team report, but let's just recapture the incident. We had a patrol in the main road going down south, and we observed smoke in the -- what's that, western side of the valley, indicating that large amounts of houses were being set on fire, and we stopped our vehicle and observed and we saw military personnel moving from one house to another, supported by a fuel truck, and setting houses on fire. It was a very methodically [sic] event or -- executed event, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That was in the Drnis area?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just south of Knin. I think that we should perhaps see the video that is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's okay. If we could go back to -- I'm sorry, my question, though, was who was with you on the trip?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stig Marker-Hansen, among others.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Who were the others?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had our driver, and I presume also Eric Hendriks. But I'm not fully sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we could back, Mr. Registrar, to D741, please. If we could go to page 10, please, which is the entry for that day, on the 10th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And I'd ask you to read through that and tell me when you finish reading the entry for the 10th of August. Have you finished reading it, sir?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, what I noted on this, sir, is that -- first of all, would you agree with me that seeing army units going house to house setting fire to homes with fuel tanks would be an event that would be a significant part of anyone's day, to observe something like that. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. In your diary, there's no reference to it and when you talk about the patrol, at the end you say: "The patrols Stig and I conduct are very good. Like the patrol up Mokro Polje, deserted camps, children's books and old tanks. A large KMT family camp, the scale of personal tragedies are very great." Now if you could explain to the Court why, for example, children's books and old tanks would make it into your diary as an event of the day but Croat troops moving from house to house with fuel tanks wouldn't have been something that you felt should be noted in your diary for the day?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, the fuel tank episode was covered in other words later, but I'll need to peruse through my entire diary. What is reflected in my diary sometimes is new events. My diary is not a complete repetition of all the activities for an individual day. Whether the inclusion of deserted camps, children books, and old armoury, I guess that it was included as it was a new event on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, I know --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did reflect on the way the patrols of me and Stig Marker-Hansen went and I think that by that time that was important in my diary for myself to note down. I would bring it to your attention that the fact that an episode, large burning, if you wish, that took place every single day throughout the entire area did not make it into our diary, or my diary everyday does not suggest that it doesn't take place. The fact we dealt with it yesterday, that it was a Croat or a Serb minority village before 1991, if your question introduces an element that if is it not in, then it isn't, then it is taking things out of context. My diary is not to be reproduced as the history. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, you do also highlight as part of the patrols this visit to the Krka monastery and you do note that: "The Krka monastery was being guarded on direct orders from General Gotovina. Thieves think alike." Can you explain to us what "thieves think alike" means in your diary?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The entry into the diary of churches being guarded while large areas were being burned at the same time, it brought home to me this odd situation where you can have complete destruction going on in a large area and suddenly you have a pinpoint where destruction does not go on. I interviewed the soldier at the gate of the monastery and I believe that some days ago we actually dealt with that issue, how I knew that it was on orders, because I asked the soldier, You're guarding here; yes, it was on direct orders from General Gotovina. Could we enter the church. No, we couldn't because he had orders to guard it. And it struck me that you can have military order protection of property totally intact, pinpoint intact, at the same time as you have intense destruction going on, and I think it was a reflection that thief think every man steal. People in that area knew that things would be burned. Therefore, you would have to guard some other things. I came across the same appearance in other churches. Let me describe the church in the Kosovo Polje which is in the -- by the way, the same area as the incident we just dealt with before, this vast burning of the entire western side of the valley, and you have one church that is kept free of destruction. Thief -- [Foreign language spoken] is a common Danish expression. I do not have the appropriate command of the English language to fully translate that proverb. I would request the translation service perhaps to assist us in [Foreign language spoken].

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Liborius, there are several daily reports including the incident in Guglete where you say you were an eye-witness and you actually recorded some plates. You say you were in Kistanje with plates, you were in Guglete with plates. Which institution of the Republic of Croatia did you refer the crimes that you had witnessed with the licence plates?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The institutions of Republic of Croatia at that time was the senior military and the military governor. I and my fellow monitors brought that to the attention, sometimes, during our meetings. Sometimes we provided factual information, saying, This car with this number plate has been seen in the area where the people in the car was doing this and this and this. Can I please ask you, institutions of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me rephrase the question. For example, the incident in Guglete where, as I read your testimony, you and Mr. Hendriks were the only eye-witnesses. You saw HV military police and an INA truck or van, you got the plates down. You say, based on circumstantial evidence you concluded that they must have set fire in the village of Guglete. You never actually then turned around and called the Croatian police or the Croatian military police and filed a report that you witnessed a crime. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military police, they were there. Do you suppose me to call them and say, Hey, boys, you just set fire to a house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The civilian police?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a nice one. Sorry. Of course we brought that to the attention in our regular meetings. We had stacks of licence plates, military units, where we said, These people are doing what we can observe everyday. Looting and burning. Why don't you do something about it. I also brought it to the attention of Petar Pasic, when he was introduced as the government representative in Knin. I sometimes asked also the police check-points why they were not stopping people who they could in the eye -- just within sight of the eye could see looting and burning. So I think that if I should recall how many times I talked to police officers or government institutions, if we take that as a broad understanding, I could fill a very, very large book. What my finding was that nothing was done to stop it. Let's apply some common sense here. You see a military police car with military police personnel where all circumstantial evidence suggests that they have lit up the house you were just at. How do you think they would react?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, my question to you then, sir, is how is the commander of the military police to react if, in fact, what you're saying is true if you don't tell him?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was -- if he didn't know that, he would be more than blind. What his reaction should have been, and now you get my assessment anno 2008, it corresponds to my assessment in anno 1995, 1996, was to take some proper action. Why not bring perpetrators to justice when they do things that are so visibly wrong. I don't recall that there is any excuse for burning and looting at large-scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I speak please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, Mr. Liborius, because it is not an answer to the question anymore.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I just want an answer to my question. Sir, you witnessed --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, he hasn't answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you report the crime in Guglete to anyone, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: That's a factual question. But before, about the military police commander, I thought that was argumentative.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, because he's arguing with me, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- let's -- Mr. Liborius, if the questions are argumentative, I invite you to seek the factual elements in the question and answer to that. Mr. Misetic, if the witness is answering in an argumentative way, I invite you to bring him back to the facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm trying, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, again, this should be a yes or no question. Did you report what you say in Guglete to any Croatian authorities?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, yes, I did, at various occasions with my notebook bring a couple of classical cases, well-documented --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I have to stop you because we're really running out of time, Mr. Liborius.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you report the plates that you saw in Guglete to the Croatian authorities, and if so, when and who?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I had meetings with, as I said, for example, Petar Pasic, I remembered at one instance we were discussing law and order and he said, Well, couldn't you provide factual evidence. And I remembered at one meeting I sat with my notebook, this one here, and took a few incidents, among them also the Guglete.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So you didn't refer it to the police. You referred it to the mayor of Knin, right?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That particular incident, I remembered that I discussed that with Mr. Petar Pasic. I do also remember that I, in discussions with police, would take some classic cases. I cannot here today say at what time of the day I did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You know Guglete is not part of Knin municipality. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. You can't recall a specific date or specific person in the police that you actually referred that incident to, as you sit here today. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: First part of your question, specific date, no, I cannot; second part of your question, specific person, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Petar Pasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Petar Pasic is not part of the Croatian police, Mr. Liborius.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that information came across very well. Mr. Liborius has testified that he specifically remembers to have reported this incident to Mr. Pasic. The location is not in Knin. Mr. Liborius has told us that he has no clear recollection on what events he specifically reported to police. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Registrar, if I can call up 1D50-0383, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. Can we please tender into evidence 4048. That was the exhibit, 10th of August, that was shown to the witness, at least that is my proposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I believe it has already been tendered by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I don't think so, no. I don't find it on my record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What again was the 65 ter number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 4048 does not --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We got an e-mail saying that you were tendering that exhibit right before the direct started from Ms. Henry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't communicate that to Chambers, that's why I would like to seize the opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, that's why we --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's why we have incomplete lists. Is it -- do you tender it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Shall we assign it a P number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit number P830.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P830 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I meanwhile ask, Mr. Waespi, have now the -- the notebooks, have they been fully transcribed yet or not, and are they in the system because -- I'm not talking about the diaries but about the notebooks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: The parts that were relevant to my examination-in-chief, yes, have been.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but the other parts. I was specifically asking about the other parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: The notebook is -- is huge. I don't think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it uploaded in e-court, the original?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We have uploaded it, Your Honour. It's the D -- D74 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but if it's not -- as long as you've uploaded it's not --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you then give me the number because --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's two parts, D743 and 744.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speakers are kindly asked not to overlap, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, this is an ECMM analysis from the 6th of February, 1995. And it talks about the capabilities of the Croatian army and the ARSK and what can be anticipated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn -- we can just flip through the first page and then turn to the second-to-last page, please. If we can scroll down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, there's an assessment for Sector South. And the ECMM assessment was: "The strategic and political importance of Knin gives to this sector capital transcendence. On the other hand," and there is an incomplete sentence, "the required ratio of forces for an offensive action could be reached." The third paragraph there: "To ensure or at least to increase the probabilities of success is required a perfect coordination with the HVO which can combine another action against the same sector from the east." "Final assessment: "Croatian army has not the capability to plan, to prepare, and," if we can go to the next page, please, "finally to conduct a general offensive operation in all the sectors, but if decides a reopening of the hostilities with some guarantees for success, the main and principal attack should pursue an important strategic political and emotional objective to be chosen. This main attack could be combined with a local diversionary one and, in any case, other sector versus to be strongly hold. "The most logical course of action in the case of an offensive operation conducted by the Croatian army would be to organise the manoeuvre as follows: 1, to conduct a diversion attack against UNPA West; 2, to reinforce and held strongly CL in UNPA north; 3, to conduct a decisive and main attack against Knin." Now, Mr. Liborius, as you were being briefed by coming back into the theatre in July 1995, you would have received this assessment. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That one from 6 February, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, you would have received an assessment that the ECMM should expect that the Croatian army -- the most logical course for the Croatian army would be to conduct a decisive and main attack against Knin. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did receive information that would suggest that a military operation would be likely. Or could not be ruled out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, did you receive information that the attack most likely would focus on Knin?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did receive information at the headquarters of the UN forces in Zagreb that preparations were in trying -- in the UN forces in anticipation of a large Croatian army operation, not only limited to the Sector South, but to the entire area of Sector North and Sector South.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, you've told us that you are a military man as well by background. Could you -- when you read the sentence that says that the Croatian army doesn't have the capability to conduct a general offensive operation and then it goes on to say: "But if it decides, the main principal attack should pursue important strategic political and emotional objective to be chosen." Based on your military background, can you interpret what is meant by choosing an emotional objective?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly can. But do you think it is the best way forward that we discuss on the basis of the 6th February meeting -- assessment way before the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, what questions to put to you and in what order is for Mr. Misetic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. An emotional objective - now you get my speculations as of today - for example, Knin as the seat of the Krajina Serb centre of power.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, the language used apparently is -- the witness says that he starts speculating about it which is, of course, not what we're seeking him to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me follow up on your answer, then. What you have offered an example of Knin being the centre of power, are you familiar with the term centre of gravity in NATO doctrine.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: A little bit, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. What is your understanding of what it means?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Centre of gravity, and please bear in mind that I'm not an operational planner, full time military, would mean that in your enemy, the segments of both political, military, defence and offensive capabilities would centre around.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if you were assessing --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But if you can read from a NATO doctrine -- I am not an operational planner in NATO staff headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And if you really seek to develop a discussion on this document, I think you should invite those who wrote it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's fine. I'm going to ask you -- I'm going to follow-up with your answer which was: What was the centre of political, military, defence, and offensive capabilities of the Krajina Serbs?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Knin area, of course, held vital command and control facilities. The corps structures, Lika Corps, Kordun Corps, and so on, would perhaps also -- perhaps not be seen as a centre of gravity but also as important elements.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender the ECMM analysis as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit number D756.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D756 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Registrar, if we can go back to D741, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, I'm going to now take you through a few entries in your diary before Operation Storm and ask you just to explain them so that we're clear on how we're supposed to interpret these entries when we're looking at them later. For July 27, which is the next page in, please. There's an entry that says: "Started with a morning briefing at the HQ UNCRO, with second in command Jordan GM. His conclusion: The war is unavoidable, prepare yourself for it." Do you recall that meeting and who it was that told you that war was unavoidable?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: 27 July.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And what was said about war being unavoidable?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That it was the assessment of the briefer there that the peace negotiations in progress were not certain to produce a peaceful outcome and that, therefore, preparations should be made for a war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we can go to the next day, 28 July, which is the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Third paragraph: "There's a depressed mood in Knin. Grahovo is now in HVO/HV hands. They're afraid of a HV attack on Knin. 100 percent mobilised. Should the children be evacuated? Tough decisions." First tell me a little bit about this issue about the children being evacuated. What is that reference?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a reference to the part of the population in that part of Krajina, and whether they should be brought to Banja Luka, to Belgrade, if they should be brought out of the RSK area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Was that your own question or did somebody ask -- you know, in a conversation did some of the local Serbs say to you, Should we evacuate our children?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that it was an issue being discussed among the local Serb population.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, the entry about "100 per cent mobilised." What does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Total mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: What do you mean by the term "total mobilisation"? Is that just referring to military-aged men, does it refer to -- what does it refer to?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The total mobilisation was the term used by the local Krajina Serb authorities for the degree of mobilisation at that time. I interpreted it so that able-bodied men were required to participate in the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Where it says: "They're afraid of a HV attack on Knin," who is the "they" that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The local population.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we can go to the next entry for the 29th of July. You have an entry that says: "RSK has now once again been declared completely mobilised. All the people and materiel are now included in the total defence." What does "all the people" refer to?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It refers to statements by the local authorities that the persons who were able should participate in the defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And what does the materiel refer to?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Materiel in Danish, is [Foreign language spoken]. You have personnel [phoen], personnel, and materiel --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Equipment, in a broader sense?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Military equipment. Yeah, broader sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now if we could turn the page and go to the entry for the 30th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I believe the witness said "military equipment," which is not recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Military equipment in the broadest sense. That's what happens if I intervene. People are speaking at the same time. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The 30th of July, there's a sentence there that says: "The interpreters are driving their children to Banja Luka, Beograd and other safe places." Can you tell us how you learned that information?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From our staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did some of your staff drive their children to Banja Luka, Beograd and other safe places?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were using their personal cars.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: What I meant was when it says "the interpreters," were they interpreters on your staff?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Right. Then there's a reference to the Patriarch Pavle, Martic, KN Dragan -- KN Dragan, does that refer to Captain Dragan?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Babic. "Yes, they were all there at the train station. Full speed on the nationalist rhetoric, the music. Martin ..." skipping on down, "The church is glowing in war rhetoric, therefore, no good is coming from there. What does that sentence mean? "The church is glowing in war rhetoric."

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That the speech of the patriarch was inflammatory, that it rejected all possibilities for co-existence between Serbs and Croats, that war was, if it came, a holy endeavour. It was nothing -- when I say no sound talk is coming from that one, it is to be understood that he was not participating or contributing to finding a peaceful way out and supporting the peace negotiations in earnest. You said music. Nationalist muziken [phoen] that is an expression. It is not music as such, it is rhetoric and speaking and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just so we're clear and there's no confusion. Patriarch Pavle is who?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the senior religious figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Of?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The church, the Serb Orthodox church.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And do you recall there being a large gathering in Knin on the 30th of July where Patriarch Pavle spoke?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I write in my diary approximately 1200 spectators, but that is my own assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: There's also a reference here it says: "Martic in battle attire, promises personally to take Grahovo back." Do you recall what he said about that?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not word by word but he certainly made words to the effect that, as far as I remember, that he would personally be leading the units going up to Grahovo and take it back and that enforced this -- this rhetoric, the reference to nationalist muziken, the nationalist overinflated rhetoric.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we can go to the next day. You talk about the points of the Akashi RSK agreement and that Tudjman demanded several things. If you can look through all of them. Your conclusion is: "Yes, so they are prohibitively high demands." Can you tell us why were Tudjman's demands prohibitively high? Which one of the demands was prohibitive or which of them, I should say?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When taken together, the demands, and let me stress that this was my analysis of how the Krajina Serbs would react, not an assessment of how I see the best way forward. Let's just keep that in mind. That the demands, the four demands that the pipeline should be operational within 24 hours, that direct negotiations about the rest of the infrastructure, especially railroad, Zagreb-Split via Knin, the Croatian constitution should rapidly be finalised so that RSK could be reintegrated peacefully into Croatia, and the first one, Tudjman demanded that he should speak with -- or negotiations could be with others than Martic. When I say, yes, there are -- what is the English translation? Yes, so they are prohibitively high demands that is to suggest that the RSK reaction to, in particular, the infrastructure parts, well, also the fourth part, they would not accept them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Speaking of the fourth part, do you think -- it was your conclusion that the Krajina Serbs would not accept that fourth element. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was my conclusion at that time as, if you wish, a political analysist [sic]. That is not to suggest that it was what I personally desired.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Of course. Now, continuing on in that entry. Second paragraph: "Otherwise today is significantly more calm than yesterday. Now the worse panic has subsided. People are now being stopped by CPs so they aren't fleeing out of RSK." "CPs" stands for what, Mr. Liborius?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Check-point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us a little bit more about where you received this information that people were being stopped at check-points so they aren't fleeing out of the RSK?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just need to find the place. Could you ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's the next paragraph after we -- the four points being prohibitively high, on the 31st of July.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it was a combination of both information from colleagues and locals.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn to the 2nd of August entry, which is page 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: 2nd of August, your diary says: "The Knin valley works like people are now in a state of war with all the uniformed men at the front. ARSK has worked hard in the most recent days in order to establish defensive lines around Grahovo." First, can you tell us where you received the information about establishment of defensive lines?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, from colleagues and from local population.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you see movement of troops or materiel on or around the 2nd of August by the RSK army?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was movement of soldiers, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we can go to the 4th of August, please, which is the next page. Towards the end it says: "ARSK in disbandment. Many losses on its account, sadly. The military leaders and political leaders seem to have disappeared." Do you recall where you got that information on the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say a lot of losses on that account, sadly, I was referring to individual persons. You should mark -- this is an full stop after ARSK is in -- what's the -- is in disbandment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking about the information that the military leaders and political leaders seem to have disappeared. Where did that information come from?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: UN colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Liborius.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Misetic. Mr. Kay, you're next.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- again, it is not any criticism, we spent a lot of time this morning on procedural matters. Of course the Chamber was involved in that as well. Even if I would deduce all of that, Mr. Misetic, you were just a little bit over the one and a half hour for the first session. Let's try, all of us, to work as efficiently as possible and you are specifically invited, Mr. Liborius, to do that as well. And the first step would certainly be to carefully listen to what exactly is asked from you. I just give an example of the last one where Mr. Misetic was not very precise, whether he asked about the information about the disbandment or the leaders not being present anymore, so parties are invited to be very price in their questions. You're invited to carefully listen to the questions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And Mr. Kay is ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, usually counsel introduce themselves. I sometimes do it. Mr. Kay is Defence counsel for Mr. Cermak. I thank you for your insistence, Mr. Liborius. I had forgotten to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you for the introduction, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, first of all I'm going to ask you some questions about the ECMM. Looking at your evidence as a whole, it seems that you were operating outside the UN structure. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hello, Mr. Kay. I was operating outside the UN structure. The ECMM had its own mandate, dated back from 1991, and it had its operations, so it was operating side by side, in some instances, vis-a-vis the UN structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We've seen an agreement in this court as an exhibit - no need to bring it up; it is called D28 - which was between Mr. Akashi, on behalf of the UN, and Mr. Sarinic, on behalf of the Croatian government. You, as a member of the ECMM, were outside that agreement. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I really have to see the agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Take it from me, you're not mentioned in it and it was a fact that I thought you may know. If you don't know, just say so.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had a standing agreement that we could draw on the UN support --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The question I asked is about the Akashi-Sarinic agreement. If you don't know anything about it, just say so.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm interested in your position. You came to Knin at the end of July. It's right that you were away on holiday from the -- about the 8th of September to the 20th of September. Is that right? I've looked at your diary and seen that you were away on holiday from the 8th of September and you stayed up in Zagreb for some days. Certainly till around the 20th of September.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was on leave 8 September, and I came back from leave 26 September, not the 20th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very, very much. And you returned from Zagreb to Knin and continued working in Knin from the 26th of September, or were you away on -- on other trips in October or November that you can recall? I don't want you to read all your diary; just if you can recall it.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did have trips to Zadar, to Split -- November. Among others. And I did return to Zagreb end of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. When the Croatian forces came into Knin on the 5th of August, did you have an established link to those forces as of -- of that date with whom you could liaise as to what was happening in Knin?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not. The HRC had meetings, and I think that it has been covered in some of the reportings with regard to General Cermak, I think. But right on the 5th, I did not myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you have any contacts prior to that date of the 5th of August with the Croatian military?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: How far back do you want to go?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just say yes or no, if you had.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prior contact with Croatian military. I recall having spoken to some Croatian army personnel in the Pleso airport before my arrival in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would it be right to characterize it then that you had no substantial or significant contact with the Croatian military before they arrived in Knin on the 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- also have meetings with Croatian personnel, Brigadier Misic, I think, back in 1994 and others of the Croatian armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It doesn't seem substantial to me. Are you able to correct the impression in any way by giving more detail? I noticed you referred to meeting some people at an airport. That doesn't sound substantial to me. Are you able to characterize it in a more precise way?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pleso airport was not an airport. Pleso airport was part of the UN operation and it had many, many peoples coming and going there. Could you please be more specific as to the character of the conduct? I'm not sure what you're --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm going to change the question, actually, to this. Did you have any in-depth knowledge of the structure of the Croatian military as of the 5th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And in what way? Perhaps you could describe it to me, what you knew about their military.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had received a number of briefings in UN format and in national format. I had, as I said, in 1994 I had a chance to discuss with senior Croatian military personnel. I would say that my general knowledge or my general understanding of the Croatian military was at a -- at a reasonable level.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, I think a list was distributed yesterday as far as the breaks are concerned. We'll continue today -- the morning until 2.00, which means that we now should take a break of 20 minutes so that we have the last part of this morning's hearing between 12.40 and 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will have a break for 20 minutes and we'll resume at 20 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could we turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, we had to discuss a procedural matter which had nothing to do with your testimony here. We apologise. I understood that you also had another matter. Yes, Mr. Liborius.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It was brought to me, for the first time, during the break, that there was apparently a requirement for me to sign a Rule 75(C) document, and it's -- I don't know all the legal articles. I was a bit surprised to learn that, and I discussed with the Witness Section what that would mean. They said that -- they believed that I had signed it and it was the first time I had heard about it. So I'm not fully aware of what the legal status then is, as I have not signed it yet. That was the reason --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me read to you Rule 75(C), and I earlier said you should discuss the matters with the Victims and Witness Section --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... you come back, so that's apparently what you did. Rule 75(C) reads: "The Victims and Witnesses Section shall ensure that the witness has been informed before giving evidence that his or her testimony and his or her identity may be disclosed at a later date in another case, pursuant to Rule 75(F)." Rule 75(C) deals with witnesses in respect of whom protective measures have been granted. Such measures often are the expunging of names and identifying information from the public records. Sometimes that these witnesses give their testimony through image or voice-altering devices or that they testify under a pseudonym. Now, what actually Rule 75(C) says is that if protective measures are granted, and I repeat, no protective measures were granted in respect of your person, although we allowed you to give a small portion of your evidence in private session, that there are legal mechanisms than always requires a decision by a Chamber, that whatever is said here in a confidential hearing should remain confidential even if that evidence, if the transcript would be used in any other proceedings, and that it's only on the basis of a decision by a Chamber that it could be made public. And apparently, I don't know whether this is misunderstood, but the information is mainly to give you a proper understanding of what the Rules in this respect say. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Now, that's -- this is not happened that I have been informed of this and I have not signed it. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I -- [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, not prior to giving testimony. I appreciate your explanations and I just have two questions. With regard to the -- you mentioned 75(F), other cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Outside this Court or in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The procedures are there for both cases in this Tribunal and sometimes material to be used in local courts as well, but then these courts have to seek permission from the Tribunal and as a general standard then the witness will be contacted to what extent he would have objections against this material to be given to, for example, a local prosecutor who might need that material for investigative purposes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So my consent would be required prior or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that's not why I ask. I asked the -- when in discussion with the Witness Section -- were the penalties associated if breach of confidentiality is done --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Would the parties agree that, where I earlier said that the Chamber is not in a position to speak with the witness, that I would have during one of the next breaks a short conversation with the witness in which I can answer questions exclusively related to this issue. Any objection such a solution? Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For my part, I don't, Your Honour. Maybe he needs the assistance of one of the Chamber's legal officers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We could also ask one of our legal officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- or a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or a lawyer, yes. Well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- our legal officers are lawyers.
